bull_bear.body: Preferential equity raise to fund capex without promoter dilution (proportionate participation); Focus on integrated value chain over M&A.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Delay in government ethanol price revision; Uncertainty on non-plastic mandate timeline (expected sooner than 6 months but not guaranteed); Crop yield dependency on monsoon (assessment possible only by Aug-Sept); PLA market adoption speed vs fossil plastic price volatility.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on PLA technical readiness and cost advantages; Cautiously optimistic on ethanol pricing ('fingers crossed'); Transparent on sugar recovery challenges (0238 variety replacement difficult).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: PLA biodegradation in Indian landfill conditions occurs within one season even if mixed with other materials; Competitors can replicate feedstock advantages but lack Balrampur's 2-year R&D headstart; Customers waiting for production commitment before switching suppliers despite validated quality.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet as on 30th June 2026: long-term borrowings of Rs. 75.25 crores for the existing business and Rs. 1086.00 crores for the PLA project.
- During Q1FY27 the company availed long-term debt of Rs. 183.00 crores for PLA capex and repaid Rs. 22.25 crores under the yearly repayment schedule of loans taken for the existing business; scheduled repayments are Rs. 66.75 Cr for the balance of FY 2026-27 and Rs. 8.50 Cr in FY 2027-28.
- PLA term loan repayment is back-ended - it commences from Q3 FY29, payable in 20 equated quarterly installments.
- Credit ratings: CRISIL long-term AA+/Stable and short-term A1+; India Ratings IND AA+/Stable and IND A1+.
- The CMD's stated philosophy: "Leveraging our operations with strong financial strength we remain dedicated to... enhancing operational efficiencies. We will continue to invest judiciously and create value for all our stakeholder."
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Sugar: Crushed 1,043 lakh quintals (+5.2% YoY), recovery 11.24% (vs 11.28%); Ethanol: Produced 27 crore liters in FY26, capacity expandable to 34-35 crore liters, shift towards B-heavy/Juice route due to volume constraints in C-heavy; PLA: First integrated plant in India, leveraging captive sugar/bagasse for cost advantage.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising fossil fuel costs and plastic mandates drive demand for bio-alternatives | Balrampur Chini Mills Ltd | beneficiary | High | First-mover advantage in integrated PLA production with captive feedstock ensures lowest cost structure globally as per management. |
| Ethanol price freeze despite high crude costs squeezes margins | Pure-play Ethanol Producers | loser | Med | Lack of integrated sugar operations makes them more vulnerable to prolonged price stagnation compared to Balrampur. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- BCML describes itself as "one of the largest integrated sugar companies in India", with allied businesses comprising distillery operations and cogeneration of power, and "one of the most efficient integrated sugar producers in the country".
- The company presently has ten sugar factories located in Uttar Pradesh with aggregate sugarcane crushing capacity of 80,000 TCD, distillery capacity of 1050 KLPD and cogeneration of 175.7 MW (Saleable).
- BCML "is also in the process of setting up India's 1st Poly Lactic Acid (PLA) plant of 80,000 TPA capacity" - the deck's stated transformation of identity beyond sugar.
- The CMD frames the model as: "Over the years, our integrated model have successfully kept pace with headwinds and adopted to evolving dynamics of the industry... focusing on maximum value creation from every stick of cane."
- Growth history is described as "well planned capacity expansion projects and the acquisition of existing companies".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [State incentive] Uttar Pradesh's Bio Plastic Industrial Policy 2024 (announced 4th October 2024) gives investors of Rs. 1,000 crore or more a 50% capital subsidy on eligible investment disbursed over 7 years after commercial production, 5% interest subvention for 7 years, 100% SGST (net) reimbursement for 10 years, electricity duty exemption for 10 years and stamp duty exemption; total incentive capped at 200% of eligible investment. Invest UP has issued a Letter of Comfort to the company approving eligibility, subject to commencement of commercial operations and stipulated conditions.
- [Subsidy condition] The capital subsidy is linked to a Gross Capacity Utilisation Multiple (GCM): GCM is 1 if actual production to installed capacity is 40% in the 1st year, and 75% in subsequent years.
- [Ethanol policy] For ESY 2025-26 OMCs have contracted ~1048.4 Cr BL of ethanol; supply till 30th June 2026 was ~717.29 Cr BL, giving blending of ~19.99% (ESY 2024-25: ~1003 Cr BL supplied till 31st October 2025 against ~1131.7 Cr BL contracted, blending ~19.24%). A roadmap for "Beyond E-20" is being worked on by the Government.
- [Feedstock policy] The government has allowed 72 lakh tonnes of FCI rice to be sold at Rs. 23.20 per kg to ethanol distilleries under the EBP programme for ESY 2025-26 - relevant to BCML's newly started rice route.
- [Associate] BCML holds 30.47% of Auxilo Finserve Private Limited (16.53 Cr shares at average cost Rs. 10.59/share, investment Rs. 175.00 crores); Auxilo's net worth as on 30th June 2026 is ~Rs. 1528.37 crores, total assets Rs. 5531 crores, GNPA 0.52%, NNPA 0.12%, CRAR 29.74%, and the value of BCML's investment basis the last equity raise is Rs. 959.40 crores.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: PLA margins protected by zero logistics cost on sugar/bagasse and captive power vs peers; Sugar margins pressured by INR 30/quintal SAP hike; Ethanol margins stagnant due to lack of price revision since FY23.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Linked to PLA commissioning in Q3FY27 and potential ethanol price revision; Margin: Targeting 35% EBITDA on PLA (excluding incentives); Order Inflow: PLA customer finalization nearing completion; Capex/Commissioning: PLA plant commissioning expected Oct 2026 (Q3), Lacto-gypsum plant approved at Kumbhi.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: PLA commercial agreements in advanced stages with multiple customers awaiting production commitment; no specific tonnage disclosed but 'progressing well' with testing complete for barrier properties.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Expansion of PLA capacity with 15-18 month execution timeline post-decision; E85/E100 ethanol blending roadmap driving future demand; Gypsum board manufacturing from PLA by-products.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Balrampur Chini navigated a 7.5% cane cost hike in FY26 via operational efficiency and volume growth, while positioning its first-of-its-kind PLA plant for imminent commercial ramp-up amid rising fossil plastic prices. The core thesis hinges on the transition from sugar cyclicality to high-margin bioplastics, supported by lowest-in-memory sugar inventory levels and anticipated government ethanol price corrections.

open.item: Co14201 variety expected ~16% of crush this year with significant increase next year, plus multiple pipeline varieties over a four-to-five-year plan.
Full-year FY26 sugar cost of production expected around Rs 37.5/kg.
FY26 sugar sales volume guided possibly ~10 lakh tonnes versus ~9.4 lakh tonnes 2-year average, on higher inventory.
Reaffirmed aspiration of 35% EBITDA margin on PLA, excluding incentives (capital subsidy and interest subvention are below EBITDA).
PLA plant to be commissioned in the third quarter of this year (Q3FY27); revised capex Rs 3,080 crore post fundraise.
At full capacity PLA revenue potential Rs 2,000 crore at peak with guided 35% EBITDA margin.
PLA project on plan for commissioning October 2026; ~90% of imported equipment arrived; cumulative spend Rs 1,421 crore (Rs 790 crore debt) as of 31 Jan 2026.
PLA topline of ~Rs 2,000 crore assumes ~$2.5/kg realisation on 80,000 tonnes; historically prices have reached $4/kg.
Goal is to sell PLA all domestically, targeting applications where per-unit cost impact is negligible; management confident of selling out 80,000 tonnes.
PLA plant will consume ~1.25 lakh tonnes of sugar (about 1.7x of 80,000 tonnes output) as feedstock at full capacity.
PLA plant expected to generate ~Rs 2,000 crore annual revenue with ~35% EBITDA margin.
At full 80,000 tonne capacity PLA project expected to generate ~Rs 2,000 crore revenue with targeted EBITDA margin of 35% plus.
PLA commissioning schedule remains on track for October 2026.
PLA plant rated capacity 75,000 tonnes per annum, targeting full utilisation with goods expected to sell from day of commercial production.
PLA project on schedule and on timeline, targeting commissioning in October 2026.
PLA project targeted for commissioning in October-November 2026, spending spread over roughly two years and three-four months from now.
Positive conversations with government on ethanol price and quantum revision have begun given crude at Rs 111 and currency at Rs 96; management thinks it will get done but stays cautious.
Anticipate 5-7% expansion in cultivated cane area for the upcoming season, driven by higher cane prices and new geography allocations.
Not expecting any loss in PLA's first year; management personal view is the business should fly from March 2027.
Management targets maximum six months to reach optimum PLA utilisation, would be disappointed if it took 1-1.5 years.

verdicts.item: Company sugar price around Rs 41/kg expected to at least maintain, with possible marginal uptick in coming months.
verdicts.note: Price maintained with uptick outlook: 'In UP, prices have broadly remained in the range of Rs. 41 to Rs. 42 per kg. We believe prices would remain steady and gradually probably inch up.'

verdicts.item: For ethanol year 2025-26 expecting ~28 crore litres of ethanol including ENA.
verdicts.note: Slightly below the 28 guide: 'in the year gone by, that is FY26, we produced around 27 crore liter of ethanol.' [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: SAP (state cane price) likely to rise, possibly for two years; recovery gains over two years hoped to offset cost increases.
verdicts.note: SAP-rise materialized ('increase of INR30 in sugarcane price from INR370 to INR400') but recovery did not rise to offset: 'gross recovery... marginally lower at 11.24% vis-a-vis 11.28%.'

verdicts.item: Management hazards next season should see some uptick in cane crushing and a decent uptick thereafter.
verdicts.note: Uptick materialized: 'The Company crushed 1,043 lakh quintals of cane during the season, which is up 5.2%.'

verdicts.item: PLA in-house production targeted for commissioning in Q3 FY27 (October 2026); Rs 927 crore spent till July-end (Rs 460 crore debt) of ~Rs 2,850 crore gross capex.
verdicts.note: Timeline holds but the Rs 2,850 cr gross capex in the item was revised up to Rs 3,080 cr. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Recovery positively inclined to rise from 11.28%, but not back to 11.72% in one year, maybe two years.
verdicts.note: Recovery did not rise as hoped: 'gross recovery... marginally lower at 11.24% vis-a-vis 11.28%'; management: 'this looks like the bottom.' [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Management positively inclined towards increase in crushing from last year's figure, subject to weather over next two months.
verdicts.note: Crushing increase realized: 'crushed 1,043 lakh quintals... up 5.2%'; UP crushed 7% lower while Balrampur crushed 5.2% higher.

verdicts.item: SAP in all likelihood to go up, possibly for two years; management hopes recovery over two years makes up for cost increases.
verdicts.note: SAP-rise prediction materialized ('INR30 in sugarcane price from INR370 to INR400') but recovery fell to 11.24% - offset not achieved in year 1.

verdicts.item: Balrampur expects a 7-8% increase in cane crushing for the FY26 season, aiding fixed cost absorption.
verdicts.note: Crushing rose but short of 7-8%: 'crushed 1,043 lakh quintals... up 5.2%.' [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: EY26 ethanol route mix: ~9 crore litres juice, ~12 crore B-heavy, ~3+ crore maize, ~3.5 crore country liquor, ~1 crore C-heavy.
verdicts.note: Broad mix executed with more B-heavy: 'we have increased our ethanol production from the B-heavy route this year'; C-heavy 'not lowered.' Detailed split not restated numerically.

verdicts.item: Company importing PLA and running trials with ~10 customers/applications to have facility sold out before commissioning; certifications factored into timeline.
verdicts.note: 'the existing converter machines are fully in sync with our product'; barrier/food-safety technicals cleared. Sold-out-before-commissioning goal not yet achieved.

verdicts.item: At current SAP with no ethanol price change, plan is ~10% of cane crush to juice route, ~25% to C-heavy, balance to B-heavy.
verdicts.note: Plan broadly executed: B-heavy increased, C-heavy not lowered; 'we had to fill our tenders in November' hoping for a price revision that did not come.

wtt.summary: 83% guidance hit (26 chains); 1/6 projects on-time; 3 expired; 16% theme consistency (info)
wtt.tone_latest: Confident and content, especially on PLA; management owned the ethanol tendering misjudgement ('once bitten, twice shy') and was candid that matching Co0238 recovery looks tough.
